title: CuTe DSL Data Types for GPU Kernels
key_concepts: Native CuTe types map directly to hardware formats
Floating-point types: FP16, BF16, FP32, FP64
Integer types: Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64
critical_patterns: Mixed-Precision GEMM: FP16 compute, FP32 accumulate
Dynamic Precision Selection: Compile-time flag for FP16/FP32
constraints: FP16 has limited range and precision
BF16 has lower precision but same range as FP32
Type mismatch errors require explicit casting
FP64 is slower on consumer GPUs
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL provides a range of data types optimized for GPU operations, crucial for tensor core operations, memory bandwidth optimization, and numerical precision management. The primary floating-point types include FP16, BF16, FP32, and FP64, each with specific use cases and hardware support. FP16 is favored for deep learning due to its memory efficiency and native tensor core support, despite its limited precision. BF16 offers the same range as FP32 but with reduced precision, making it suitable for large model training. The introduction of Float8 types (E4M3 and E5M2) on Hopper+ architectures allows for extreme performance gains, particularly in large language models. Integer types, such as Int8 and Int4, support quantized neural networks, with tensor core operations providing significant throughput improvements. Type conversions and promotions follow standard rules, with explicit casting necessary to avoid type mismatch errors. Mixed-precision patterns, such as computing in lower precision and accumulating in higher precision, are common in deep learning. Architecture-specific support varies, with Ampere and Hopper architectures offering enhanced performance for various data types. The decision tree for type selection prioritizes correctness, hardware support, performance, and memory footprint, ensuring optimal use of resources. Debugging type issues involves careful attention to type assignments and conversions, with tools available for runtime type checking. CuTe DSL's interoperability with frameworks like PyTorch is facilitated through type mapping and DLPack conversion, ensuring seamless integration. Performance considerations highlight the importance of choosing the lowest precision that maintains accuracy, balancing memory bandwidth and compute throughput. Overall, CuTe DSL's data types and patterns enable efficient and precise GPU kernel development, aligning with modern hardware capabilities and performance demands.
